selfApproval: withheld. I authored the content and every revision pass.

partA_contentFix.before: Why was the presentation shorter than planned?
partA_contentFix.after: What reason does the speaker give for how long the presentation ran?
partA_contentFix.mechanismOfTheLeak: The old stem ASSERTED, before any audio, that the presentation departed from plan. LST_Q_009's key is 'A technical problem spoiled their plan' - the same proposition, down to the shared word 'plan'. One of Q009's four options therefore became the obvious answer with the clip hidden.
partA_contentFix.whyStemOnly: The assertion lived in the stem. Options, key, key index, distractor rationales, subskill (inference) and tier (D4) are all unchanged, and LST_CLIP_04's script is byte-identical, so no TTS cost is incurred.
partA_contentFix.answerRationaleUpdated: It referenced the same presupposition ('shorter duration') and now reads 'the length the speaker reports'.
partA_contentFix.assertedGuards: The new stem is asserted free of the tokens plan, shorter, short, problem and technical.

perClipReview.method: All stems and options of each clip read together with the scripts hidden, then against the script. Semantic reasoning, not word-overlap.
perClipReview.CLIP_04_reasoning: The stem now asserts only that the speaker commented on duration. A learner holding that fact has no basis to prefer 'A technical problem spoiled their plan' over the applause, slides or audience options. In the other direction, none of Q009's options mentions duration or cutting, so Q010's key is not cued either. Both items still require the audio: Q009 needs the deflection, the projector failure and the memory fallback combined; Q010 needs 'I cut the part I was least sure about'.
perClipReview.residualRecorded: LST_Q_010 option 1 still reads 'They were given less time than planned'. It retains the word 'planned', but it is an OPTION - one hypothesis among four - not an assertion, and if it were true it would COMPETE with Q009's key (an externally shortened slot is not a technical problem). Left unchanged under the stem-only preference and recorded here rather than hidden.

models.attemptReadiness: DiagnosticAttempt already carries resultState, overallScore (documented to stay null and never 0 while any skill is incomplete), and version pinning via scoringVersion / blueprintVersion / contentVersion.

partB_architectureAudit.reusableFromOtherModules: R2 object storage, BullMQ/Redis background jobs, the Gemini grading client and the Azure Speech path are already in use by the standalone Speaking module and are called by the diagnostic Speaking/Writing services. Do not build duplicates.
partB_architectureAudit.oneCanonicalFlow: There is no V1-vs-V2 learner UI split to remove. /diagnostic is already the single learner route and getCurrentAssessment serves whichever assessment is current. V1 is DATA, not a parallel flow, so the canonical experience is reached by replacing content and fixing four contracts - not by deleting code.

correctedAssumption.what: I expected V1 to store the rich options object that getQuestionMeta reads. It does not.
correctedAssumption.evidence: Read-only query on DiagnosticQuestion returns a plain array: ["At noon", "At the train station", "Near the main entrance", "At the café"]. A jsonb_object_keys call on it errors with 'cannot call jsonb_object_keys on an array'.
correctedAssumption.consequence: getQuestionMeta's object branch - which carries section, passageText, audioUrl, stableKey, construct and questionType - is fully implemented but nothing currently writes that shape. So V1 has no audio or passage delivery either, which matches the handoff's note that V1 has no genuine Listening audio.
correctedAssumption.whyItMatters: It makes D4-013 a defect in MY Step 2C4 mapper rather than in the runtime. The mapper writes options as string[], which reproduces V1's limitation exactly. The minimal correct fix is for the importer to write the OBJECT form, which needs no schema change and no runtime change because sanitizeQuestion already derives audioUrl for LISTENING and passage text for READING from that metadata.

D4_011.verified: isActive Boolean @default(true) and status @default(ACTIVE). grep for a read path filtering on status returns 0; four read paths filter on isActive: true (diagnostic.service.ts:527, 599, 616, 706) and getCurrentAssessment orders by id desc. The schema comment calling status authoritative is not implemented, so statusOnCreate DRAFT has no effect on serving and OMITTING isActive is the failure mode.
D4_011.secondConsequence: getCurrentAssessment calls assertQuestionBank before returning, so an assessment that fails validation makes GET /diagnostic/current throw for every learner, not only V2 takers.
design: the importer sets isActive:false AND status:DRAFT explicitly in the same statement that creates the row, in the same transaction as its questions - never relying on defaults
read paths select on status = ACTIVE as the authority, keeping isActive in sync during the transition rather than dropping it
activation becomes a separate explicit operation gated on a readiness check
a validation failure on a non-current assessment must never break the current one: scope assertQuestionBank to the assessment being served and fail closed to the previous ACTIVE row
D4_011.constraint: Use the existing DiagnosticAssessmentStatus enum. No new state invented.

D4_012.verified: validateQuestionBank branches on meta.questionType. OPEN_TEXT requires stableKey && section && construct && intendedLevel, and getQuestionMeta populates intendedLevel ONLY for ['A1','A2','B1','B2'] (diagnostic.logic.ts:157). Everything else requires values.length >= 2 and correctIndex in range. So a productive task can only validate by persisting a CEFR code, which V2 forbids and the mapper correctly refuses.
D4_012.design: One task-type-aware validator, not a V1/V2 pair. The discriminator is the taskType COLUMN - never correctIndex, never option count. MCQ requires 4 unique options, exactly one key in range and resolving references; LISTENING additionally requires a clip reference and the audio delivery contract; READING a passage reference; SPEAKING_RESPONSE a prompt, prep/response seconds and a resolving rubricVersion; WRITING_RESPONSE a prompt, word bounds and a resolving rubricVersion. The intendedLevel requirement is dropped outright - it is a CEFR field this product does not claim.
D4_012.forbidden: No fake options, no correctIndex -1 standing in for an MCQ, no fake key, no CEFR code to satisfy an obsolete validator.

D4_013.design: The importer writes the OBJECT form into options, carrying values, questionType, section, passageText, audioUrl, stableKey and construct. No schema change, no runtime change; it reuses the delivery code that already exists.
D4_013.rejectedAlternative: Migrating sanitizeQuestion to the dedicated V2 columns and the DiagnosticListeningClip relation. Correct long-term but a larger change than the goal requires now.
D4_013.confidentialityUnchanged: sanitizeQuestion returns a 12-field allowlist containing neither correctIndex nor explanation, and the clip script is not in the returned shape at all. That must stay true.

GAP_1.partialAnswerFound: The options object carries stableKey, which getQuestionMeta already reads and validateQuestionBank already requires for OPEN_TEXT. Writing draftKey there costs nothing and needs no migration - but a value inside a Json column cannot carry a database unique constraint, so it gives app-level identity, not a guarantee.
GAP_1.note: All nullable, all additive, V1 rows stay valid. A stable question key alone is insufficient - passages and clips duplicate on re-run without their own. Import must be one transaction: passages and clips, then rubrics, then questions, then the assessment in its final DRAFT state. A failure must leave nothing active.
GAP_1.notAppliedHere: Schema migration and canonical persistence belong to a later authorised phase.

OBJECTIVE_PERMUTATION.verifiedFailureMode: Five production call sites, not two: diagnostic.logic.ts:305 and diagnostic.service.ts:343, 823, 1048, 1096. At :1048 and :1096 perm is `attemptId && !isOpen ? getAttemptQuestionPermutation(...) : undefined`, gated on an OPTIONAL client-supplied attemptId. When absent the function falls through to `answer === question.correctIndex`, comparing a DISPLAY index against an AUTHORED index. It fails open and mis-grades silently.
fixPlan: resolve the permutation from authoritative server-side attempt state, looked up by the attempt the submission belongs to, never from a client parameter
for an MCQ with more than one option a missing or invalid permutation becomes an error, not a fallback; return a discriminated cannot-grade rather than a boolean
tests must invoke isDiagnosticAnswerCorrect itself across all 24 permutations plus correct, incorrect, missing permutation, invalid permutation, missing attempt, wrong owner and duplicate submission
toResult returns selectedOption (display) beside correctOption (authored) with no marker; return both in one frame or drop the index fields for the text fields
OBJECTIVE_PERMUTATION.selfCriticism: My Step 2C4 permutation suite asserts perm[displayed] === correctIndex, which is a tautology about the array and never calls the grader. It must be replaced, not extended.

designs.productiveGrading: DiagnosticSpeakingService handles confirmRecording, skip, list and ownership-scoped audio retrieval, with DiagnosticSpeakingAudioNormalizer converting webm/opus to 16k mono wav. DiagnosticWritingService handles enqueueMany and retry asynchronously. Both call the existing R2, BullMQ and Gemini infrastructure. Controller routes exist for speaking confirm/skip/list/audio and writing retry. This is reusable as-is; the work is wiring it to V2 content and to DiagnosticSkillResult.
